Bletchley Park -- why it matters
recentItems.description: A short film prepared for Bletchley Park's new visitor centre, sharing a personal perspective on Bletchley's continuing importance by Megan Smith, VP Google[x].

recentItems.title: Mailüfterl: an Austrian star of European computing
recentItems.description: In the 1950's, a group of Austrian students led by Heinz Zemanek designed and built the Mailüfterl, one of the earliest fully transistorized computers.  For a brief moment, this "Viennese spring breeze" put Austria at the vanguard of European computing.  This film produced by Google tells the story.  More details here: http://googleblog.blogspot.co.uk/2013/10/an-austrian-star-of-european-computing.html

recentItems.title: Margaret Marrs shares her story
recentItems.description: Margaret Marrs was senior computer operator for EDSAC, the first 'practical' stored program computer in the UK.  Produced by Google as part of a series of short films highlighting women's involvement in the early days of computing.

recentItems.title: Mary Coombs shares her story
recentItems.description: Mary Coombs was a programmer for LEO, the Lyons Electronic Office that was the world's first business computer.  Produced by Google as part of a series of short films highlighting women's involvement in the early days of computing.

recentItems.title: Joyce Wheeler shares her story
recentItems.description: Joyce Wheeler was a researcher at Cambridge University who was among the earliest to use EDSAC, the first 'practical' stored program computer in the UK. Produced by Google as part of a series of short films highlighting women's involvement in the early days of computing.

recentItems.title: Freelance Programmer: the story of Dame Stephanie Shirley
recentItems.description: In 1962 Dame Stephanie Shirley founded one of the UK's first software startups, dedicated to employing women software developers working part-time from home, which went on to be hugely successful.  In this film she shares her inspirational story.  Produced by Google as part of a series of short films highlighting women's involvement in the early days of computing.

recentItems.title: Q&A with Vint Cerf
recentItems.description: This was filmed on 1st July at Google, as part of an event celebrating the UK's computing heritage. Earlier Vint had spoken about the early days of the Internet.  In this Q&A he primarily focuses on its future.

recentItems.title: The birth of the Internet in the UK
recentItems.description: A conversation between four of the early pioneers describing how they brought the Internet to the UK.  Filmed on 1st July at Google, as part of an event celebrating the UK's computing heritage.  Speakers include Roger Scantlebury and Peter Wilkinson, who worked at  the National Physical Laboratory and helped develop the NPL network, the first internet like thing in the UK.  They were joined by Peter Kirstein, then from UCL and Vint Cerf, at that time at UCLA/Stanford/DARPA.  As well as describing what they did, context is given to the NPL's role and to the political and bureaucratic challenges at the time.

recentItems.title: Manchester Baby: world's first stored program computer
recentItems.description:
This video was produced by Google as a tribute to the "Manchester Baby"—the first computer to run a program electronically stored in its memory. This was a flagship moment, described by some as the "birth of software".  To find out more see: http://googleblog.blogspot.co.uk/2013/06/youve-come-long-way-baby-remembering.html

While nothing remains of the original machine, a working replica is on display at MOSI (Museum of Science & Industry, Manchester). For more information about MOSI and demonstration times of The Baby visit www.mosi.org.uk

recentItems.title: WEIZAC: Israel's first computer
recentItems.description: A short film sharing Professor Aviezri Fraenkel's story of working on the team who built WEIZAC, the first computer in Israel.  Film produced by Asher Tlalim with support from Google.
